meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: at the regular payday for the pay period in which separation occurred
facts.summary: Indiana: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due at the regular payday for the pay period in which separation occurred.
facts.evidence_quote: Sec. 2. (a) Whenever any employer separates any employee from the pay-roll, the unpaid wages or compensation of such employee shall become due and payable at regular pay day for pay period in which separation occurred

facts.value: not required until the next usual and regular payday
facts.summary: Indiana: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due not required until the next usual and regular payday.
facts.evidence_quote: if an employee voluntarily leaves employment, either permanently or temporarily, the employer shall not be required to pay the employee an amount due the employee until the next usual and regular day for payment of wages, as established by the employer.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Indiana basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Applicable to employers of 2 or more employees Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $7.25 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Indiana independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): No
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.value: Employers must report within 20 days of an employee's hire or re-hire date.
facts.summary: Indiana new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Employers must report within 20 days of an employee's hire or re-hire date.
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Employers must report within 20 days of an employee's hire or re-hire date.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: Indiana: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Bi-weekly; Semi-monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.value: At least semimonthly, or biweekly if requested
facts.summary: Indiana pay frequency rule: At least semimonthly, or biweekly if requested.
facts.evidence_quote: shall pay each employee at least semimonthly or biweekly, if requested, the amount due the employee.
facts.notes: Wages must be paid to a date not more than 10 business days before payment (same section).

facts.summary: Indiana is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
